display.title: Episode 506: The Secret Tunnel (After Chanukah)
display.summary_short: Right after Chanukah: the few who beat the many, a Shema guest from Madrid, the story of an old shamash and the menorah that hid a secret tunnel, and a letter about helping for Shabbos.
display.summary_long: Broadcast just after Chanukah. Uncle Yossi explains the lesson of 'the many in the hands of the few': our enemies come with chariots and horses, but we come in the name of Hashem, and we stay on Hashem's side by learning Torah and doing mitzvos. Every Jewish child's neshamah is a little menorah, kept lit all year by mitzvos. After the Hakochainik march, an eleven-year-old boy visiting from the Chabad House in Madrid leads the Shema and tells about receiving a dollar and a brachah from the Rebbe, and everyone gives tzedakah. Story time: Reb Beryl, an aged shamash, lovingly polishes the great brass menorah beside the Aron HaKodesh and finally reveals why. When he was young, hooligans with swords surrounded the shul, and the rabbi turned one of the menorah's arms to open a secret tunnel through which everyone escaped. A mother's letter tells how her daughter helps prepare for Shabbos, a fine example of kibbud av va'em. Uncle Yossi teaches that Torah and mitzvos are light that shows good from bad, encourages girls to light Shabbos candles with a gift offer, and gives candle-lighting times.
display.lesson: Hashem is on our side when we are on His side; Torah and mitzvos are the light that keeps our neshamah burning and shows us good from bad.

date.note: 'Right after Chanukah'; one week after episode 505. Chanukah 5752 ended 2 Teves (9 Dec 1991); Tuesday 3 Teves fits, as do candles 4:11.

advisories.note: In the story, Jews are kept from learning Torah and armed hooligans attack shuls; many lives were lost in such attacks.
Armed hooligans surround a shul and give the worshippers ten minutes to pray; all escape.

privacy.note: The Shema guest and the letter writer's daughter are named in full on air.

sources_cited.note: 'These with chariots and those with horses, but we in the name of Hashem.'
'Rabbim b'yad me'atim', the many in the hands of the few.
'Ki ner mitzvah v'Torah or': mitzvos and Torah are light.

segments.title: After Chanukah: The Few Against the Many
segments.summary: We win because we come in Hashem's name; keep the little menorah of the neshamah lit all year with Torah and mitzvos.

segments.title: Shema with a young guest from Madrid
segments.summary: A boy visiting from the Chabad House in Madrid leads the Shema and tells about his brachah from the Rebbe.

segments.title: The Secret Tunnel
segments.summary: An old shamash reveals how the shul's great brass menorah opened a secret tunnel that saved the congregation from armed hooligans.

segments.title: Uncle Yossi's Mailbox: Helping Mommy for Shabbos
segments.summary: A mother writes how her daughter helps prepare for Shabbos, and Uncle Yossi praises her kibbud av va'em.

segments.title: Torah and mitzvos are light
segments.summary: Light shows what is good and what is harmful; Torah and mitzvos show us the difference.

segments.title: Lighting Shabbos candles
segments.summary: Girls are encouraged to start lighting Shabbos candles, with a gift and a brachah chart offered by mail.
